title: Indian Party System: Dominance to Coalitions

scenes.text: How did one party dominate India before regional coalitions took over?
scenes.narration: Have you ever wondered how India went from one party ruling everything to a colorful web of coalition governments? Here is the secret behind how our democracy evolved.

scenes.text: One star captain decided everything before regional players demanded shared team leadership.
scenes.narration: As an everyday analogy, imagine a school cricket team. At first, one superstar captain makes all the decisions, but eventually players from every neighbourhood demand a say and form a joint leadership council.

scenes.name: Rajni Kothari
scenes.idea: Congress acted as a consensus umbrella with opposition parties exerting pressure.
scenes.narration: Scholar Rajni Kothari called India's first phase the Congress system. Congress functioned as a broad party of consensus accommodating everyone, while opposition parties acted merely as peripheral parties of pressure.

scenes.heading: Breakdown of One-Party Dominance

events.what: Non-Congress governments formed in eight states
Vajpayee NDA government completes full term
Congress suffers defeat across key states

scenes.narration: Here is how power shifted across eras. After 1967, Congress lost control of several states, and by 1989, coalition politics became a permanent necessity to run the central government.

scenes.heading: Rise of Regional Parties
steps: Power centralises in party high command
scenes.narration: Notice how one event triggered the next. When Congress centralised power at the top, regional leaders broke away to build regional parties, transforming India into a competitive multi-party democracy.

scenes.heading: Western Versus Indian Coalitions
scenes.narration: Professor Vidyut Chakrabarty highlights a sharp contrast with the West. Western democracies form coalitions by design around shared philosophies, but Indian coalitions are tactical calculations formed mainly to keep opponents out of power.

items: Congress system functioned as an umbrella party of consensus.
Centralisation and democratic upsurges birthed powerful regional parties.
Coalition politics is an inevitable reflection of Indian diversity.
scenes.narration: Always remember these three takeaways. India moved from an umbrella consensus to regional empowerment, making coalition governance a natural reflection of our country's incredible diversity.
